newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German machine maker Sket to be broken up.
newsitem.headline: East German machine maker Sket to be broken up.

text.p: Sket GmbH, the former East Germany's biggest heavy machinery group, said Thursday it would undergo massive restructuring and shed nearly a third of its work force.
Managing director Werner Kirchgaesser told reporters that it was necessary to spin off Sket's steel rolling mills, cable and wire plants and oil divisions into separate companies.
Kirchgaesser, formerly head of Kloeckner-Humboldt-Deutz AG, was speaking after a meeting of the money-losing machinery maker's supervisory board.
Breaking up the company into independent parts would lead to the loss of 600 jobs from a work force of 1,850.
Management said the restructuring plan could bring the company back into profitability by the end of 1998. It expects a loss of around 190 million marks ($125 million) this year.
The supervisory board will make a final decision about the restructuring on Oct. 14.
